steps.name: Sample structure QC and outlier characterization
caveats: Do not remove sample_03 in this step; only characterize it.

steps.question: Does sample_03 (flagged as separating from the rest of its group on PCA and the sample-distance heatmap) show a technical explanation — abnormal library size, detected-gene count, or other QC metric — and how does the full 10-sample cohort structure (5 treated vs 5 control) look under blind VST-based PCA and sample-distance clustering?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: blind vst, PCA on top-500-variance genes, sample distance heatmap, per R-0033; outlier investigated for technical cause before any decision, per R-0034.

constraints: Use raw counts (not pre-normalized) as DESeq2 input.
VST must be run with blind=TRUE for this QC step.
steps.description: Load the 12000x10 raw Salmon gene-level count matrix and the 10-sample metadata (condition: treated/control). Apply DESeq2's variance-stabilizing transformation blind to the design, compute PCA on the top 500 most-variable genes, and draw a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap, coloring by condition. Report library size (total counts) and number of detected genes per sample. Specifically characterize sample_03's departure from its group: whether it is explained by markedly low/high library size or detected-gene count, or whether it appears to be a genuine biological outlier with no stated technical cause. Do not remove any sample at this step — only characterize and report findings that will support the removal/retention decision in the DE step.
acceptance_criteria: PCA plot and sample-distance heatmap produced for all 10 samples, colored by condition
Library size and detected-gene-count table produced per sample
A stated conclusion on whether sample_03's departure has an identifiable technical cause or not

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: primary (all 10 samples) and sensitivity (sample_03 excluded) fits
caveats: n=5 per group is below the 7-replicate threshold for DESeq2 count-outlier replacement, so a flagged count outlier gets an NA p-value, not a replaced value — report how many genes are affected by this apart from independent-filtering NAs.
Do not select genes by unadjusted p-value or by fold change alone; use padj<0.05 as the selection rule.
The two fits will differ; this is expected and must be reported as a sensitivity comparison, not resolved by picking whichever gives more hits.
steps.question: Which genes differ in expression between treated (n=5) and control (n=5) muscle samples, and how much does that gene list depend on sample_03 — the sample that separates from its group on PCA/sample-distance QC?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage per R-0001/R-0009; outlier sample kept-vs-excluded dual fit and reported per R-0067/R-0090 since the smallest group (n=5) exceeds the 3-replicate down-weighting threshold; minimal pre-filter (10 counts / smallest group size=5) per R-0002/R-0029; explicit reference level and BH+independent filtering at alpha 0.05 per R-0036/R-0010.

constraints: Pre-filter: keep gene if count>=10 in at least 5 samples, applied before both fits.
Apply apeglm shrinkage using the treated-vs-control coefficient (not ashr, since this is a single-coefficient contrast).
Use DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization internally; do not pre-normalize counts.
steps.description: Pre-filter to genes with at least 10 counts in at least 5 samples (the smallest group size). Build a DESeqDataSet with design ~condition, explicitly setting 'control' as the reference level. Fit DESeq2's Wald test on the FULL 10-sample cohort (primary analysis) and, as a sensitivity analysis, refit on the 9-sample cohort with sample_03 excluded. For both fits, keep DESeq2's built-in count-outlier handling (Cook's distance flagging with NA p-values, since n=5 per cell is below the 7-replicate threshold for count replacement) switched on. Apply apeglm shrinkage to the condition (treated_vs_control) log2 fold change for both fits. Extract results with independent filtering at alpha=0.05, and inspect the raw p-value histogram before trusting the BH-adjusted values. Name the full-cohort fit the primary result per the stated no-removal-without-cause principle unless T1S1 established a clear technical cause for sample_03's departure — state explicitly in the output which fit is treated as primary and why, referencing the T1S1 finding.
acceptance_criteria: Two DESeq2 result tables produced (10-sample and 9-sample-without-sample_03), each with baseMean, log2FoldChange (unshrunken), apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, pvalue, padj
Reference level of condition explicitly set to 'control' and contrast documented as treated vs control
p-value histogram inspected and reported for both fits
Number of genes tested after filtering and number significant at padj<0.05 reported for both fits
Explicit statement of which fit is primary and the stated reason

steps.name: Overlap and divergence between primary and sensitivity DE gene lists
caveats: This step is descriptive comparison, not a new statistical test — do not compute a new p-value for 'change of status'.
steps.question: How many genes are called differentially expressed (padj<0.05) in both the full 10-sample fit and the sample_03-excluded 9-sample fit, and which genes change significance status when sample_03 is excluded?

grounding.reason: Outlier sample removed/retained sensitivity comparison: report both fits, the intersection, and genes that change status, per R-0090.

steps.description: Compare the two DESeq2 results tables from T1S2. Compute the intersection and the set difference of significant genes (padj<0.05) between the full-cohort and sample_03-excluded fits. For genes that change status, report their padj and shrunken log2FoldChange in both fits side by side. Produce a simple overlap visualization (e.g., Venn/UpSet-style counts) and a table of discordant genes.
acceptance_criteria: Table of genes significant in both fits (padj<0.05), with counts
Table of genes significant only in the full-cohort fit and only in the sample_03-excluded fit
Overlap summary numbers (n intersection, n each fit) reported

steps.name: Preranked GSEA (Hallmark, then Reactome) on primary fit's Wald statistic
caveats: Ranking by the Wald statistic (not unshrunken log2FC alone, not a signed p-value) is a stated, disputed methodological choice — report it explicitly.

MSigDB Hallmark human (2026.1) is present in the reference store at /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-hallmark-human/2026.1/ and Reactome pathways at /mnt/refs/managed/reactome-pathways/current/ — use these directly rather than any live download.

If fewer than ~50 genes are significant at padj<0.05, do not additionally run an over-representation test on that short list; the ranked fgsea result on the full list is the primary enrichment evidence.
steps.question: Which coordinated biological pathways or processes (MSigDB Hallmark; then Reactome as follow-up) are enriched among genes ranked by their treated-vs-control DESeq2 Wald statistic, in the primary (full 10-sample) fit?

grounding.reason: Preranked fgsea on full tested-gene list against Hallmark then Reactome, ranked on the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stated choice per disputed rule R-0108), per R-0107/R-0048/R-0098; size window 15-500 and redundancy collapse per R-0047/R-0052; leading edge reported per R-0105.

constraints: Use the full ranked list of tested genes (post low-count filter), not a significance-thresholded subset, as fgsea input.
Apply gene set size filter of 15-500 members among tested genes.
Use BH adjustment for pathway-level multiple testing.
steps.description: Map gene symbols in the primary DESeq2 results table (T1S2, full-cohort fit) to Entrez IDs using org.Hs.eg.db, reporting the share of tested genes that fail to map or map ambiguously. Rank all tested genes (post pre-filter, pre significance-cutoff) by the DESeq2 Wald statistic ('stat' column) as the enrichment ranking metric — stating this choice explicitly since the ranking-metric choice is disputed in the literature. Run fgsea against the MSigDB Hallmark human gene set collection (50 sets) with min/max set size 15-500 and BH adjustment; then run a follow-up fgsea pass against the Reactome human pathway gene sets (filtered to Homo sapiens) with the same parameters. Collapse redundant significant pathways (fgsea::collapsePathways). Report the leading-edge genes for each significant pathway in both collections.
acceptance_criteria: Gene symbol-to-Entrez mapping performed with unmapped/ambiguous share reported
fgsea run on the full ranked gene list (not a thresholded subset) using the Wald statistic
Hallmark and Reactome fgsea result tables produced with NES, padj, and leading-edge genes
Redundant significant pathways collapsed
Gene set size window (15-500) and collection versions stated in output

Report includes the sample_03 overlap/divergence summary from T1S3

plan.title: Muscle treated vs control DE with outlier sensitivity
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 10 samples: 5 treated vs 5 control, muscle tissue, single unpaired batch), with sample_03 flagged as an outlier on PCA and the sample-distance heatmap. Per grounded knowledge-service rules, an outlier is never dropped silently: it is investigated for a technical cause first, then either down-weighted (if a sufficiently replicated group permits) or removed only with a stated criterion, and the DE analysis is run and reported both with and without it. The flow is: (1) sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library-size/detected-gene diagnostics) to characterize sample_03's departure; (2) minimal pre-filtering and DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization; (3) an explicit two-group model (condition: treated vs control, control as reference) fit twice — full 10-sample cohort (primary) and a sample_03-excluded sensitivity cohort — with Wald testing, apeglm LFC shrinkage, and BH-adjusted independent filtering (alpha 0.05); (4) preranked fgsea against MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome, ranked on the DESeq2 Wald statistic; (5) an integrative report comparing the two DE gene lists (overlap, discordant genes), the two enrichment results, and stating which fit is primary and why.

steps.method: vst(blind) PCA, sample distance heatmap, library size QC
Keep genes with >=10 counts in >=5 samples (smallest group size)
DESeq2 Wald test, primary=all 10 samples with sample_03 down-weighted via robust dispersion / sensitivity refit without sample_03
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, Hallmark then Reactome
Report with both fits (with/without sample_03), overlap of gene sets, MA/dispersion plots, leading edge genes
